claims.statement: The coach persists application-owned member records in the LangGraph BaseStore under the closed namespace ("users", user_id, collection); the permitted collections are metrics, injection_log, reminders, feedback, upload_registry, profile, episodic, ops, events, and gate.

validate_user_namespace() binds every store helper to exactly the requesting user's namespace and an allowlisted collection, raising StoreNamespaceError otherwise; persisted values are privacy-scrubbed with _scrub_json(), re-validated against the typed model, and written with index=False.

guard_user_write() rejects ordinary store writes whenever the member's ("users", user_id, "gate")/"erasing" record exists, raising ErasureGateError, which prevents concurrent normal writes during self-erasure.

Schedule state is not stored directly; approved ApprovalEvent records are read in (created_ts, event_key) order via schedule_state() and folded into active ScheduleEntry values through Add, Reschedule, and Cancel mutations.
append_event() is idempotent by op_id: a repeated append with the same op_id returns the existing stored event rather than creating a duplicate.

A reschedule or cancel event whose target entry_id is absent or already inactive in the folded schedule state is persisted with decision declined-stale instead of approved, leaving derived schedule state unchanged.

POST /coach/uploads reads the request body into a bytearray via read_multipart_upload(), requires exactly the fields upload_id, thread_id, and one file, and rejects payloads once the buffer exceeds MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES plus a 64 KiB multipart overhead allowance, clearing the buffer before raising.
Upload admission accepts only PDF, JPEG, or PNG, requiring the declared MIME type and filename extension to agree, and the maximum accepted file size is 10 MiB (MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES).

post_upload() additionally checks the file's byte signature against its declared MIME type via _valid_file_signature() before proceeding, so MIME type, filename extension, and content signature must all agree.

The multipart reader does not use framework multipart spooling; it accumulates the whole request into a bytearray and clears it in a finally-equivalent path both on success and on rejection, so raw bytes are not retained beyond the request.

post_upload() verifies the authenticated member owns the target thread (via a self-call GET on /threads/{thread_id}) before creating a deterministic reservation thread keyed by reservation_id(upload_id), with owner and intended_thread metadata and a 15-minute TTL (UPLOAD_TTL_MINUTES).

Repeating the same upload reservation returns its current stage only when the existing reservation's metadata matches the new request; a conflicting reservation on the same upload id with different metadata is rejected.

UploadRegistryRecord tracks status through uploading, scanning, extracting, and either done or error, stores a privacy-scrubbed proposal and non-content metadata (never raw upload bytes), and carries separate consumed and admitted flags.

get_upload_registry() enforces that the record's owner matches the requesting user_id (raising StoreNamespaceError otherwise) and treats a record whose expires_at has passed as absent, deleting it under the write gate and returning None so status lookups distinguish missing from expired uploads.

The member perimeter admits an attachment for a run only once by setting the registry record's admitted flag to true rather than consumed, after rechecking owner, intended thread, completion status, and expiry; this lets the graph make the first claim while a resend is denied at the perimeter.

claim_document() derives user_id and thread_id from graph configuration, accepts only a non-expired, completed (status=="done"), unconsumed registry record bound to that thread and containing a proposal, and otherwise returns the same DOCUMENT_UNAVAILABLE re-upload message instead of recovering document data.

claim_document() hashes the canonical claim data (user_id, thread_id, attachment_id, proposal) into an idempotent pending OpRecord via put_op_if_absent(), clears the attachment from graph state, and routes to review_document.

review_document() first deletes the upload registry entry for the claimed attachment, then relies on the persisted OpRecord for interrupt and replay behavior; if the operation has already reached a terminal (non-pending) status it returns the saved result instead of re-applying the decision.

On an accepted document review decision, each selected field is passed through sanitize_memory_field() before a profile record is written; a declined decision writes no profile facts, and a field that fails sanitization is discarded and marked with a privacy notice rather than saved.

A ReminderRecord stores an owner-scoped reminder id, title (1-80 chars), weekday, HH:MM local time validated by TIME_PATTERN, an IANA timezone validated via ZoneInfo, an active flag, an optional remote cron id, originating thread id, wake token, and next-run date; create_reminder() enforces a cap of MAX_ACTIVE_REMINDERS (10) active reminders per user across all threads.

edit_reminder() rotates the reminder's wake_token on every edit via secrets.token_urlsafe(32); soft_cancel_reminder() performs a soft cancel by setting active=False and clearing cron_id rather than deleting the record.

Reminder creation is two-stage: create_reminder_impl() persists an inactive record, creates the remote cron via CronClient, then finalizes the record as active with the returned cron id and next run date; a definite create failure leaves the local record inactive.

When a create or update has an ambiguous network outcome (CronAmbiguousError), the implementation searches remote crons by member and reminder metadata via CronClient.search(), reconciles to one canonical cron, and deletes duplicates.

An edit that fails after rotating the wake token (edit_reminder_impl's pause-then-update/create sequence) leaves the rotated record inactive rather than reactivating it, preventing a stale credential or cron from authorizing an old scheduled wake.

A delivery wake carries reminder id, member id, thread id, and wake token; coach_gate() only looks up the stored reminder record (and thus can only validate the wake) when the calling principal is not in member role/context, so a wake presented in member context is always routed to short_circuit rather than delivery.

reminder_delivery() independently re-validates the wake by requiring a valid, active stored ReminderRecord whose reminder_id, thread_id, and wake_token (compared with hmac.compare_digest constant-time comparison) all match; an invalid wake is cleared without producing a message, and a valid wake yields a reminder card without any model or memory access and never exposes the wake token.

cancel_reminder_impl() pauses local state (soft_cancel_reminder) before deleting the recorded cron and any remote cron matching the reminder's metadata via _delete_all_for_reminder(); incomplete remote cleanup causes it to return the CANCEL_FAILED retryable-failure message instead of confirming cancellation.

cleanup_user_crons() deletes every known reminder cron, searches for metadata-orphaned crons owned by the user, deletes those too, and returns success only when a final search for that user's crons is exactly empty.

sweep_upload_reservations() deletes owner-filtered reservation threads and their upload_registry records, then returns success only when both a follow-up reservation search and a follow-up registry search for that owner are empty.

For ordinary thread deletion, prepare_thread_deletion() places a cleanup_pending marker in the member's gate namespace, pauses reminders bound to that thread, and removes matching remote crons before allowing the thread deletion; a cleanup error (paused count mismatch or non-2xx/404 cron delete) leaves deletion retryable rather than deleting the thread first.
A recognized erasure request is routed by the model-free coach gate (is_erase_request()) to erase_my_data(), which first writes ("users", user_id, "gate")/"erasing" before any cleanup begins.

erase_my_data() uses the deployment cron client to run cleanup_user_crons() and sweep_upload_reservations() for all known and orphaned member crons and upload reservations, then calls delete_all_for_user() with the module-private coordinator_capability(), and always removes the erasing gate record in a finally block regardless of outcome.

delete_all_for_user() requires the caller to present the private _EraseCapability sentinel (raising ErasureCapabilityError otherwise), enumerates and validates every namespace under the member's users/{user_id} prefix before deleting anything, then deletes every item from every allowlisted namespace except gate; a malformed namespace fails validation before any deletion begins.

The gate namespace is intentionally excluded from delete_all_for_user()'s deletion loop, and the erasing marker within it is removed only afterward in erase_my_data()'s finally block, so the erasing gate outlives the bulk of erasure cleanup by design.

erase_my_data() emits the erase_confirmation_v1 AIMessage marker only when both cleanup_user_crons() and sweep_upload_reservations() report exact-zero remaining resources (clean_crons and clean_reservations both true); otherwise it returns no confirmation message, and any exception still clears the gate via finally while surfacing as a failed graph run.

The two-phase erasure design covers metrics, injection logs, reminders, feedback, upload registry entries, profile and episodic memory, operation records, and schedule events (all non-gate store namespaces) plus remote crons and upload reservation threads, but intentionally excludes the transient erasing gate record from the bulk deletion pass, removing it only after cleanup completes.

scripts/forget_member.py implements phase two of erasure: it waits for the erase run to reach stream EOF or a non-busy thread status (wait_until_terminal), verifies the erase_confirmation_v1 marker from the stream or current thread state, snapshots every owned thread id before deleting any (snapshot_thread_ids), deletes sorted non-current threads, and deletes the marker-bearing current thread last (delete_snapshot).

In scripts/forget_member.py, a missing erase marker, a polling timeout while the erase run stays busy, or a thread deletion failure stops the procedure (raising ErasureFailed or DeleteFailed) before all threads are removed; because the current thread is deleted last, an unfinished run leaves the marker-bearing thread as a retry boundary.

The remote cron and upload reservation client targets LANGGRAPH_API_URL (default http://localhost:2024) and authenticates service calls with LANGSMITH_API_KEY (as x-api-key) and COACH_INTERNAL_TOKEN (as x-internal-token); upload reservation calls in uploads.py use the same internal credential headers.

Focused test coverage for this lifecycle spans tests/agent/test_store_data.py (namespaces, sanitizer failure, event folding, reminder limits, expiry, write gates, capability-protected paginated deletion), tests/agent/test_documents.py (bounded non-spooled parsing, raw-buffer release, claim/review replay, scrubbing, invalid attachment rejection), tests/agent/test_reminders.py (inactive-first scheduling, reconciliation, failure states, validated delivery, erasure cleanup), and tests/test_forget_member.py (marker latch, polling, thread snapshot, fail-stop deletion order).
